title: Throwing a stoneware cruet set
subtitle: Matching salt and pepper pots thrown on the wheel with stopper holes and cork fit
excerpt: A matched salt and pepper cruet set , two tall, narrow stoneware pots with a hole in the base for filling and a cork stopper. The holes in the lids are pierced at leather-hard: three small holes for pepper, larger holes for salt. Both pots are thrown to matching dimensions from a single ball of clay divided in two.
sourceNotes: Stoneware cruet set throwing pattern derived from first principles.

glossaryTerms.definition: The stage for piercing the dispensing holes and the filling hole
First firing to cone 06 (approx 1000 degrees C)
Pyrometric measure of heat-work. Cone 6 approx 1220 degrees C

content.text: Silica dust is the chronic studio hazard. Silicosis is irreversible. Mix wet whenever possible. Wear a P100 respirator any time raw glaze powders are open. Wet-clean only: no sweeping, no dry sanding indoors. Adequate ventilation when firing. Do not open a hot kiln below 80 degrees C.

The cruet set challenge is dual: throwing two matching forms (the matched-production skill) and piercing clean dispensing holes at leather-hard without cracking the wall (the precision skill). The base filling hole is sized for a standard wine bottle cork, which is easy to source.

materials.name: Two small corks (wine bottle corks work well)

content.text: Weigh and wedge two balls of 220 g each. Throw each to a narrow cylinder: 90 mm tall and 50 mm diameter. Walls should be 6-7 mm thick. Leave the rim flat (no flaring). Leave a thick dome top rather than opening all the way through , the dispensing holes will be pierced later.
Collar the neck in slightly above the midpoint to give the pot a gentle waist , this makes it easy to grip. Use the chamois to smooth the rim. Wire off and allow to dry to leather-hard.

stage, use the needle tool to pierce the dispensing holes in the top domed surface of each pot. For the pepper pot: 3-4 holes, 4 mm diameter, arranged in a triangle. For the salt pot: 5-6 holes, 5-6 mm diameter. Clean each hole inside and out with a damp finger.

On the base of each pot, pierce a single 20 mm filling hole , size it against your cork. The pot is filled by inverting it over a bowl of salt or pepper, filling through the base hole, then pressing the cork in.
06. Glaze outside surfaces with mop brush, leaving the base and foot-ring bare. Glaze-fire to cone 6 (1220 degrees C).

rows.problem: Top dome is too thick to pierce easily
rows.cause: Walls were not pulled thin enough; the top dome retains clay from the initial opening
rows.fix: During throwing, use a sponge to clean the inside base and remove excess thickness from the floor of the closed-top form.

rows.problem: Holes in one pot are larger than the other
rows.cause: Hole size varies by how hard the needle tool was pressed
rows.fix: Use a dedicated tool , a metal tube punch, a skewer of known diameter , as a hole-cutter rather than a freehand needle.
